The word that won't come Walking into a room, forgetting why Losing the thread of your own sentence The name of someone you've known for years

Most people file these under getting older, or being busy, or not sleeping enough. Often that's exactly what they are.

But here's what almost no one gets told: the same experiences can be the first visible edge of changes that started quietly ten or fifteen years earlier. And many of the things driving them are ordinary, measurable, and correctable — insulin resistance, sleep apnea, thyroid function, B12, chronic inflammation, hormone shifts. None of these are dementia. None of them show up on a standard annual physical. All of them affect how your brain works today.

insulin resistancesleep apneathyroidB12inflammationhormones

You also don't need a family history. Most people who develop Alzheimer's disease didn't have one.

The question isn't whether you should be frightened. It's whether you'd rather know than guess.

The Thing Most People Get Wrong

“Almost everyone believes dementia is genetic luck — that you either drew the card or you didn't, and there's nothing to be done either way.”

That belief is costing people years of their lives. Genetics account for a small fraction of the risk. The large majority comes from factors that can be measured and changed: how your body handles blood sugar, how well you sleep, what your inflammation is doing, what your hormones are doing, what you've been exposed to.

90% of the risk factors for cognitive decline are modifiable.

Not modifiable someday. Modifiable now, with what we can measure this month.

This isn't wishful thinking. It's a genuine shift in the research over the past decade, and most people haven't heard about it yet.

“I thought PEAK was for people who already have memory problems.”

It's the opposite. By the time cognitive changes are obvious enough that family members notice, the underlying process has usually been building for fifteen or twenty years. PEAK is built for the window before that — the years when you feel fine, and the changes are still quiet, still measurable, and still within your influence.

PEAK is built for you if:

You're in your 40s, 50s, or 60s and feel healthy — and you'd rather have data than assumptions about the next thirty years
You've noticed small things and told yourself it's just age. It might be. You'd like to know for certain.
You watched a parent or grandparent decline and refuse to simply wait and see
You have no family history and have assumed that means you're safe
You know or suspect you carry APOE4, or have never been tested
You're managing blood sugar, blood pressure, sleep problems, or stubborn weight, and no one has explained what those have to do with your brain
Your labs keep coming back "normal for your age" and that has never actually satisfied you

PEAK may not be the right starting place if:

You or a loved one already carries a dementia diagnosis requiring daily care. Please call us anyway — that's a different conversation, and we'd like to have it with you.
You're looking for a supplement protocol or a single test. PEAK is six months of sustained, guided change. It works because of that, not in spite of it.

They decided not to wait and see.

The patients who do best in PEAK share one thing, and it isn't age or genetics or how healthy they were when they started. Not sure where you fall? That's exactly what the consultation is for.

What Usually Changes First

The main reason to protect your brain is decades away. That is a hard thing to stay motivated by, and we are not going to pretend otherwise. So here is what tends to happen sooner.

The fog lifting Afternoon crash easing Sleep that restores Feeling like yourself

By around three months, most of our patients describe the same handful of things: the fog lifting, thinking that feels sharper, the afternoon crash easing off, sleep that actually restores them. Not a dramatic transformation — more the steady sense of feeling like themselves again.

Something we did not expect: most people end up genuinely enjoying the way they eat. They arrive braced for deprivation and find the opposite. That matters more than it sounds, because the changes that last are the ones you are not white-knuckling.

We see it in the numbers too. Blood sugar, cholesterol, and NAD+ commonly move in the right direction well before the six months are up.

A patient pull quote belongs here once written authorization is on file — left out for now.

Not everyone experiences these on the same schedule, and some people notice less than others. But the benefit twenty years out is not the only benefit. Most patients feel the difference long before we can measure the part that matters most.

What If the Testing Finds Something?

Some people avoid this kind of testing for exactly this reason. Not knowing feels safer than knowing. That instinct is human and we understand it.

Here is the honest answer. An elevated marker is not a diagnosis. It is the earliest signal available to us, and it arrives at the point where there is still a great deal you can do about it. If your testing shows something, that is the program working, not failing — it is the entire reason to test while you feel well.

And you will not learn it from a portal message or a letter in the mail. You will hear it sitting across from your own physician, who will already have looked at everything and already have a plan for what comes next.

Nobody Ever Asks Us This

Patients ask about their cholesterol, their blood pressure, their weight. In sixty years of combined practice, almost no one has asked us how to protect their brain.

Not because they don't care. Most people care about it more than anything else on that list — they've just been told, in a hundred quiet ways, that it isn't something you get to influence.

We know that belief well. For most of our careers, we were the ones repeating it. We followed the standard protocols. We prescribed the same medications. We reassured patients with the same empty words — this is just a part of aging, there is nothing we can do.

Then we watched our own parents fade. Both of us. We felt the powerlessness as their personalities, their purpose, and their connections disappeared, and we carried the exhaustion and the caregiving and the cost of it.

“I lost someone I loved deeply to dementia — and I promised myself I would spend my career making sure that didn't happen to anyone else I could reach.”

— Dr. Lori King

That lit a fire in us. We went looking for answers — intensive training, longevity certification, years inside the brain-specific research. What we found was that most of what drives cognitive decline is modifiable, measurable, and begins decades before anyone notices a symptom. Almost none of it was in the medicine we had been practicing.

We are near the end of two long medical careers. What we do with the rest of them is not complicated: help as many people as we can prevent this. It is not just our profession anymore. It is the legacy we want to leave.

What PEAK Costs, and Why It Works This Way

If you're one of our Timarron Family Medicine patients, you're used to a copay. PEAK is different, and we'd rather explain that plainly than let you find out at the end of a consultation.

PEAK is not billed through insurance. It can't be. Insurance pays for treating disease once it arrives — it does not pay for the advanced testing, the genetic analysis, the protocol development, or the six months of physician time that prevention actually requires. Filing insurance would mean building a program around what a payer will approve rather than around what the evidence says works. We weren't willing to do that.

So PEAK is cash-pay, and we're transparent about what it costs.

depending on how deep you want the testing to go

Every version includes the complete program: the four-marker brain biomarker panel, comprehensive lab and metabolic testing, all 26 weekly modules, monthly face-to-face visits with Dr. Lori or Dr. Chris, and direct physician messaging whenever you need us. The higher tiers add professional cognitive performance testing, toxin burden analysis, and genetic analysis. Supplements are not included. We'll walk you through which one fits at your consultation.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why can't I just ask my regular doctor about this?
For many of you, we are your regular doctor — which is why we can answer this honestly. A standard fifteen-minute visit billed to insurance was never built to include four-marker brain biomarker testing, a full root-cause work-up, or six months of physician time. That's a limitation of the payment model, not of the physician. PEAK exists as a separate program to do the work a normal visit can't.
What is cognitive longevity?
Cognitive longevity is the practice of protecting how your brain functions for as long as possible — not by waiting for a diagnosis, but by identifying and addressing the measurable, modifiable factors that drive decline years before symptoms appear.
How is this different from a traditional doctor's visit?
A traditional visit is short, symptom-driven, and built around insurance billing codes. PEAK is six months long, starts with advanced testing rather than a checklist of complaints, and gives you direct, ongoing access to the physician building your protocol.
Do I have to live near Southlake? How does the virtual program work?
No. PEAK is built to work virtually. Testing is done largely from home, and your monthly visits with Dr. Lori or Dr. Chris happen over video. Patients join us from outside Southlake regularly.
Why isn't this covered by insurance?
Insurance pays to treat disease once it's diagnosed — it doesn't pay for the advanced testing, protocol development, or physician time that real prevention requires. Filing insurance would mean building PEAK around what a payer approves rather than what the evidence supports, and we weren't willing to do that.
What if I'm already a Timarron Family Medicine patient?
PEAK is a separate program from your regular Timarron Family Medicine care, with its own testing, protocol, and schedule of visits. Being an existing patient doesn't change the cost or process, but it does mean you're already working with a physician you know.
How much time does this take each week?
About an hour a week for the module itself — that's the reading and thinking it through. The action steps live inside the life you already have: what you eat, how you sleep, how you move, rather than added on top of it.
What happens at the consultation, and why does it cost $350?
The consultation is a full hour, one to one, with Dr. Lori or Dr. Chris — not a coordinator, not a sales call. It's the first hour of the work itself. The $350 is credited in full toward your program if you enroll, and it's refundable up to 48 hours before your appointment.
What is the health history form, and how long does it take?
It's a detailed intake covering ground a standard visit never touches — sleep, stress, diet, exposures, medications, and family patterns. It takes about thirty minutes and you'll complete it before your consultation.
What happens after the six months?
You finish with a PEAK Graduation Session — a full look at what changed and what's next. Most graduates continue with us into PEAK Ascent, our year-two program, but that's a conversation for after you've seen your own results, not before.
Do I have to take supplements?
Not necessarily — your protocol is built around what your testing actually shows. For some patients that includes targeted supplementation; for others the priority is sleep, nutrition, or movement. Your physician will walk you through what's recommended for you and why.

Four Brain Biomarkers, From a Blood Draw

Most brain-health programs never look directly at the brain. We do — with four blood biomarkers that together give a picture of what is happening in your nervous system right now:

p-Tau 217 — the most reliable blood marker we have for Alzheimer's-type changes in the brain
Amyloid beta 42/40 ratio — whether amyloid is accumulating, and to what degree
NfL (neurofilament light) — a signal of nerve cell injury anywhere in the nervous system
GFAP — a measure of inflammation in the brain's support cells

No single one of these tells the whole story. Read together, they tell us whether anything is happening beneath the surface — years before it would show up in how you think or feel.

Most people go their entire lives without ever knowing where they actually stand. You don't have to be one of them.

At six months, you finish with a PEAK Graduation Session — a full look at what changed and what comes next. Most graduates continue with us into PEAK Ascent, our Year 2 program. That's a decision for later, not now.
